/casper-va/bookkeeping.add:
What a bookkeeping VA handles day to day

  • Matching bank and credit card transactions to the right accounts.
  • Attaching receipts and chasing missing ones from your team.
  • Creating and sending invoices, then following up on overdue ones in your name.
  • Entering bills and preparing a list of payments for you to approve.
  • Keeping vendor and customer records current.
  • Closing the month so your accountant gets clean books and a short list of questions.

Tools a bookkeeping VA commonly uses

Bookkeeping assistants commonly work in QuickBooks Online or Xero, receipt capture apps like Dext or Hubdoc, bill pay tools, payroll platforms and spreadsheets for reconciliations. Access is set up so they can record and prepare, while payments stay under your approval.

How the first weeks with a bookkeeping VA usually go

  1. Setup. You grant accounting-software access, share your chart of accounts and explain how you categorize common expenses.
  2. Shadowing. The VA reconciles a past period while you or your accountant review the work and correct category choices.
  3. Owning tasks. Weekly reconciliation, invoicing and month-end prep move to the VA, and you review a short summary instead of the raw transactions.

Who a bookkeeping VA fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits owners who are behind on their books, small businesses that send many invoices and companies whose accountant spends too much time cleaning up records before tax time.

A bookkeeping VA records and organizes. They don’t replace a licensed accountant or CPA for tax filing, tax planning or audits, so keep your accountant for that. If your backlog is general data rather than financial records, hire a data entry specialist. If you mainly need help with bills mixed into a busy inbox, an executive assistant may fit better.

faq.q: Is a virtual bookkeeping assistant the same as an accountant?
faq.a: No. A virtual bookkeeping assistant keeps day-to-day records accurate. Your accountant still handles tax returns, tax advice and financial statements that need a licensed professional.

faq.q: Can a bookkeeping VA pay my bills?
faq.a: They can prepare bills and payment batches, but we recommend you or a manager approve and release payments. That keeps money movement under your control.

faq.q: Can a bookkeeping VA catch up months of old transactions?
faq.a: Yes. A catch-up usually starts with the oldest open month and works forward, then shifts to weekly upkeep once the books are current.

/casper-va/content-writer.add:
What a content writer handles day to day

  • Writing service and landing pages that answer buyer questions in plain language.
  • Drafting blog posts and guides from briefs, interviews or recorded calls with you.
  • Writing email newsletters and follow-up sequences.
  • Turning one long piece into social captions, short scripts and ad copy.
  • Editing your team’s drafts for clarity, length and tone.
  • Updating old posts with fresh details so they stay useful.

Tools a content writer commonly uses

Content writers commonly work in Google Docs, a style guide, your website CMS such as WordPress or Webflow, grammar and readability checkers, SEO briefs and your email platform. Many use call recordings or interview notes to capture your expertise in your words.

How the first weeks with a content writer usually go

  1. Setup. You share your audience, offers, examples of writing you like and topics you know well.
  2. Shadowing. The writer drafts a few pieces, and your edits teach them your voice and the claims you are comfortable making.
  3. Owning tasks. The writer works from a content calendar, interviews you for source material and delivers drafts that need fewer edits each round.

Who a content writer fits, and when to hire someone else

A dedicated writer fits businesses that know what they want to say but never find the time to write it, and teams that publish regularly across web, email and social.

If your pages exist but aren’t ranking because of technical or on-page problems, hire an SEO virtual assistant. If what you need is posting and community replies more than new writing, a social media VA fits better.

For a managed program, see content marketing and email marketing. Stuck for topics? Try the content idea generator.

faq.q: What should I prepare before I hire a content writer?
faq.a: Gather a short list of your offers, the customers you want and a few pieces of writing you like. Access to past sales calls or customer emails helps the writer learn how buyers talk.

faq.q: Can a content writer write about technical subjects?
faq.a: Yes, with access to an expert. Short interviews with you or your team give the writer accurate material, and you review drafts for technical accuracy.

faq.q: Does a content writer use AI tools?
faq.a: Many writers use AI for outlines or research, if you allow it. Every draft should still be written, checked and edited by the writer before you see it.

/casper-va/customer-service.add:
What a customer service VA handles day to day

  • Working the support inbox and help desk queue in order of urgency.
  • Answering live chat during your business hours using your approved answers.
  • Processing refunds, exchanges and order changes within the limits you set.
  • Escalating billing disputes, angry customers and technical issues to the right person with full context.
  • Updating your FAQ and saved replies when the same question keeps coming in.
  • Tagging tickets so you can see what customers ask about most.

Tools a customer service VA commonly uses

Customer service reps commonly work in help desks like Zendesk, Freshdesk, Gorgias or Help Scout, live chat widgets, shared inboxes, phone or VoIP systems, and store or billing platforms such as Shopify or Stripe for order lookups.

How the first weeks with a customer service VA usually go

  1. Setup. You share your policies, refund limits, tone of voice and the questions customers ask most.
  2. Shadowing. The rep drafts replies for review and handles simple tickets while you watch the queue.
  3. Owning tasks. The rep runs the queue day to day and sends you only the escalations and a short weekly summary of common issues.

Who a customer service VA fits, and when to hire someone else

A customer service VA fits businesses where support tickets, chats or calls are pulling owners or salespeople away from their real work.

If your inbound conversations are mostly sales inquiries that need qualifying and booking, an outsourced SDR is the better fit. If the tickets come from your own staff with tech problems, hire a remote IT support engineer.

An AI chatbot can answer simple questions after hours and hand the rest to your rep. If calls are going unanswered, see our missed call text back setup.

faq.q: Can a customer service virtual assistant answer phone calls?
faq.a: Yes. Phone support works through your VoIP system or a forwarded line, and the rep follows the same scripts and escalation rules as email and chat.

faq.q: How do I keep my brand voice consistent with an outsourced rep?
faq.a: Give the rep saved replies, a short tone guide and examples of good answers. Reviewing a sample of tickets during the first weeks catches drift early.

faq.q: Can one customer service VA cover email, chat and phone?
faq.a: Often, yes, if volume is moderate. When chat and phone both get busy at once, it may make sense to split channels or add a second person.

/casper-va/data-entry.add:
What a data entry specialist handles day to day

  • Entering new records from forms, emails, PDFs or paper scans into your CRM or database.
  • Merging duplicate contacts and fixing inconsistent names, phone formats and addresses.
  • Updating deal stages, order status or inventory counts as your team reports changes.
  • Cross-checking entries against the source so errors don’t pile up.
  • Building and maintaining clean spreadsheets for reports your team relies on.
  • Flagging records that look wrong instead of guessing.

Tools a data entry specialist commonly uses

Data entry specialists commonly use Excel or Google Sheets, CRMs like HubSpot or Salesforce, form tools, PDF readers and basic import tools. Many are comfortable with lookups, filters and data validation rules that catch mistakes before they spread.

How the first weeks with a data entry specialist usually go

  1. Setup. You define the fields that matter, the formats you want and where the source data comes from.
  2. Shadowing. The specialist works on a sample batch while you spot-check accuracy and confirm the rules.
  3. Owning tasks. Daily intake and cleanup move to the specialist, with a simple log of what was added, changed or flagged.

Who a data entry specialist fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits teams whose CRM or spreadsheets are out of date because no one has time to keep them current, and businesses with steady intake from forms, orders or paperwork.

If the records are financial, such as bank transactions and invoices, hire a virtual bookkeeping assistant. If data entry is only one part of a broader admin load, a general VA may cover it.

If the same data is typed in again and again, part of it can often be automated with AI automation. Once records are clean, marketing analytics becomes far more reliable.

faq.q: What kind of accuracy can I expect from a data entry virtual assistant?
faq.a: Accuracy depends on clear rules and good source data. We set up spot-checks during the first weeks so you can see the quality before handing over full volume.

faq.q: Can a data entry specialist clean up an old, messy CRM?
faq.a: Yes. A cleanup project usually starts with deduplication and standard formats, then moves into ongoing upkeep so the mess doesn’t come back.

/casper-va/executive-assistant.add:
What an executive assistant handles day to day

  • Running your inbox to a rule set: what they answer, what they summarize and what waits for you.
  • Building your week around priorities, protecting focus blocks and handling reschedules with outside parties.
  • Preparing briefing notes before meetings and capturing action items after.
  • Booking travel end to end, with an itinerary you can read on your phone.
  • Following up with clients, partners and your own team on commitments you made.
  • Pulling together weekly reports, slide decks or board packets from the data you already have.

Tools an executive assistant commonly uses

Executive assistants commonly work in Gmail or Outlook, shared calendars, scheduling links, video meeting tools, a notes or docs system like Notion or Google Docs, and travel booking sites. Many also use a CRM or project tool so they can see where deals and projects stand.

How the first weeks with an executive assistant usually go

  1. Setup. You walk through your priorities, key relationships, travel preferences and anything the EA should never touch.
  2. Shadowing. The EA sits in on meetings, drafts replies for your review and learns how you make decisions.
  3. Owning tasks. Your EA starts handling scheduling and follow-ups on their own and brings you a short daily list of decisions only you can make.

Who an executive assistant fits, and when to hire someone else

An executive assistant fits founders, owners and senior leaders whose calendar and inbox now decide their week, and who need a trusted person to speak for them on routine matters.

If your needs are mostly simple admin with little stakeholder contact, a general virtual assistant is enough. If the real problem is projects slipping across a team, hire a virtual project manager instead.

Want to estimate what an EA frees up? The ROI of a dedicated VA page lays out how to think about it.

faq.q: What does a virtual executive assistant do that a regular VA doesn’t?
faq.a: A virtual executive assistant manages your priorities, not just your tasks. They protect your time, prepare you for meetings and handle communication with clients and partners in your name.

faq.q: Can an executive assistant handle confidential information?
faq.a: Yes, with the right setup. You control access through your own accounts and permissions, and you decide which folders, inboxes and topics are off-limits.

faq.q: Should my EA be in my timezone?
faq.a: For most leaders, yes. Scheduling and same-day follow-ups go smoother when your EA works the same hours you do, and we match for that.

/casper-va/graphic-designer.add:
What a graphic designer handles day to day

  • Designing ad creative in the sizes each platform requires.
  • Building social post templates your team can reuse without breaking the brand.
  • Laying out sales sheets, proposals, case-study PDFs and slide decks.
  • Preparing print files for signs, flyers, vehicle wraps and trade-show materials.
  • Creating simple web graphics, banners and email headers.
  • Keeping a tidy asset library so files are easy to find and reuse.

Tools a graphic designer commonly uses

Graphic designers commonly use Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign, Figma for web and interface work, Canva for templates your team can edit, and shared asset folders or brand portals.

How the first weeks with a graphic designer usually go

  1. Setup. You share your logo files, colors, fonts, past designs you like and any brand rules.
  2. Shadowing. The designer works on a few small requests while you give feedback on style and turnaround expectations.
  3. Owning tasks. Requests move through a simple queue, and the designer builds templates so routine pieces get faster over time.

Who a graphic designer fits, and when to hire someone else

A dedicated designer fits businesses with a steady flow of design requests, such as ads, social, sales materials and print, that currently wait on freelancers or end up done by whoever has a free hour.

If you mainly need posts published and comments answered, hire a social media VA. If the bottleneck is the words rather than the visuals, a content writer is the better hire.

If you need a one-time project instead of ongoing support, see logo design, brand style guides or graphic design services. The free brand kit generator is a quick place to start.

faq.q: What does a virtual graphic designer need from me to start?
faq.a: Your logo files, brand colors and fonts, plus a few examples of designs you like. If you don’t have brand rules yet, the designer can help put a basic set together.

faq.q: Who owns the designs a dedicated designer creates?
faq.a: Your business does. Source files are saved in your shared folders so you keep them if anything changes.

/casper-va/it-support.add:
What an IT support engineer handles day to day

  • Working the help desk queue: password resets, login problems, frozen apps and printer setup.
  • Setting up accounts, email and software for new hires, and removing access when people leave.
  • Managing Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace users, groups and licenses.
  • Pushing updates and checking that laptops are patched and backed up.
  • Supporting staff over remote sessions and walking them through fixes.
  • Writing short how-to guides so the same questions stop coming back.

Tools an IT support engineer commonly uses

Remote IT support engineers commonly use the Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace admin consoles, Entra ID or Active Directory, remote access tools, device management platforms like Intune, ticketing systems and password managers.

How the first weeks with an IT support engineer usually go

  1. Setup. You share an inventory of users, devices and software, plus admin access and a list of known pain points.
  2. Shadowing. The engineer takes simpler tickets, documents your environment and confirms how you want requests submitted.
  3. Owning tasks. The engineer runs the queue and onboarding or offboarding, and brings you a short list of recurring problems worth fixing for good.

Who an IT support engineer fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits growing teams without in-house IT whose staff lose time to tech problems, and businesses whose “IT person” is an employee with another full-time job.

If your issues are with cloud networks, VPNs or site-to-site connections, hire a cloud network engineer. If the main concern is threats, compliance and protecting data, a remote security engineer fits better. On-site hardware work is not part of this role.

Not sure you need a person? Read do I need an IT person, or compare with managed IT services. For larger needs, see IT staffing.

faq.q: What does a remote IT support engineer do that managed IT doesn’t?
faq.a: A remote IT support engineer is one dedicated person who learns your team and systems. Managed IT is a service package that covers monitoring and support through a shared team.

faq.q: Can remote IT support set up new employee laptops?
faq.a: Yes, if the laptops can be enrolled in device management or reached remotely. Unboxing and plugging in still happens on your end.

/casper-va/jr-dev.add:
What a junior developer handles day to day

  • Making routine website and app updates: copy, images, forms and small layout changes.
  • Fixing simple, well-defined bugs from the issue tracker.
  • Updating plugins, packages and dependencies, and checking nothing broke.
  • Running manual tests on new features before release.
  • Writing small scripts and spreadsheet automations.
  • Keeping documentation and setup notes current.

Tools a junior developer commonly uses

Junior developers commonly work with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Git, a code editor like VS Code, a CMS such as WordPress or Shopify, browser developer tools and an issue tracker.

How the first weeks with a junior developer usually go

  1. Setup. You give access to repositories and a staging site, plus a short list of starter tasks.
  2. Shadowing. The developer pairs with a more senior engineer, and every change gets reviewed before release.
  3. Owning tasks. Routine updates and simple fixes move to the junior developer, while review stays in place for anything that touches core features.

Who a junior developer fits, and when to hire someone else

A junior developer fits teams with a senior developer who is buried in small tasks, and businesses with a steady list of website or app updates.

If you need new features or integrations built with little supervision, hire a mid-level developer. If the real need is testing before releases, a remote QA engineer is the better fit.

A junior developer works best with someone senior to review their work. If you don’t have that, consider application maintenance, custom app development or IT staffing for a blended team.

faq.q: Should I hire a junior developer if I have no other developers?
faq.a: Usually not. A junior developer does best with a senior person reviewing their work. Without one, a mid-level developer or a managed service is safer.

faq.q: What tasks are a good first assignment for a junior developer?
faq.a: Content updates, small bug fixes and dependency updates on a staging site are good starting points. They are low-risk and teach the codebase quickly.

/casper-va/lead-gen.add:
What a lead generation VA handles day to day

  • Turning your ideal customer profile into search filters by industry, company size, location and job title.
  • Building lists from LinkedIn, industry directories, association member pages and company websites.
  • Finding and verifying email addresses and phone numbers so outreach doesn’t bounce.
  • Adding useful context, such as recent hires, funding news or new locations, to each record.
  • Removing duplicates, current customers and do-not-contact entries before handoff.
  • Uploading clean lists to your CRM or outreach tool in the format your team uses.

Tools a lead generation VA commonly uses

Lead generation researchers commonly use LinkedIn Sales Navigator, data and enrichment tools like Apollo or ZoomInfo, email verification tools, Google Sheets and a CRM. Each list is tied to a written profile, so the research stays on target.

How the first weeks with a lead generation VA usually go

  1. Setup. You describe your best customers, the titles you sell to and the companies to skip.
  2. Shadowing. The VA builds a small sample list, and you mark which records are a fit and which aren’t.
  3. Owning tasks. List building runs on a steady schedule, and the VA adjusts the filters as your sales team reports what converts.

Who a lead generation VA fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits sales teams who do their own outreach but waste selling time on research, and companies opening a new market or vertical.

If you need someone to also send the emails, make the calls and book meetings, hire an outsourced SDR. If your list already exists and just needs cleaning, a data entry specialist is a closer match.

For a managed program, see B2B lead generation services or account-based marketing when you sell to a short list of named accounts.

faq.q: How does a lead generation virtual assistant decide who to research?
faq.a: They work from a written ideal customer profile you approve, covering industry, size, location and job titles. Your feedback on early lists tightens it further.

faq.q: Do lead generation VAs contact the prospects?
faq.a: Not by default. Their job is research and list quality. Outreach is the SDR’s role, though some teams combine both.

/casper-va/marketing-mgr.add:
What a marketing manager handles day to day

  • Turning sales goals into a quarterly marketing plan with clear owners and dates.
  • Deciding where the budget goes across channels and moving it when results change.
  • Briefing and reviewing work from writers, designers, ad specialists and outside vendors.
  • Building a simple weekly dashboard tied to leads and revenue, not just clicks.
  • Running launches for new offers, events or campaigns from plan to post-mortem.
  • Meeting with sales to check lead quality and fix the handoff.

Tools a marketing manager commonly uses

Marketing managers commonly use Google Analytics, a CRM such as HubSpot, ad platform dashboards, reporting tools like Looker Studio, project boards in Asana or Monday, and email marketing platforms.

How the first weeks with a marketing manager usually go

  1. Setup. You share goals, past results, current vendors and budget limits. The manager reviews every active channel.
  2. Shadowing. They observe how marketing and sales work together today and propose a short plan for your sign-off.
  3. Owning tasks. They run the plan, manage the people doing the work and report weekly on what is working and what to stop.

Who a marketing manager fits, and when to hire someone else

A virtual marketing manager fits companies spending on marketing with no one person accountable for results, and owners who are tired of directing every vendor themselves.

If you mainly need hands-on ad management, hire a PPC and performance marketing specialist. If the gap is daily posting, a social media VA is the better spend.

A marketing manager works well alongside a full-funnel marketing strategy, marketing analytics and, for B2B, demand generation.

faq.q: What does a virtual marketing manager own that a marketing assistant doesn’t?
faq.a: A virtual marketing manager owns the plan, the budget split and the results. An assistant carries out tasks inside a plan someone else sets.

faq.q: Can a marketing manager manage my existing agency?
faq.a: Yes. Many teams use the manager to brief, review and hold outside vendors to agreed goals, which keeps the owner out of the weeds.

/casper-va/mid-dev.add:
What a mid-level developer handles day to day

  • Building features from tickets, from database changes to the screens users see.
  • Connecting your systems through APIs and webhooks, such as CRM to billing or forms to the database.
  • Writing automations and scripts that replace manual work.
  • Fixing bugs and writing tests so they stay fixed.
  • Taking part in code review and estimating upcoming work.
  • Documenting how new pieces work for whoever touches them next.

Tools a mid-level developer commonly uses

Mid-level developers commonly work with Git, a code editor like VS Code, JavaScript or TypeScript, Python, PHP or C#, frameworks such as React, Node.js or Laravel, SQL databases, API tools like Postman and an issue tracker.

How the first weeks with a mid-level developer usually go

  1. Setup. You provide repository and environment access, a local setup guide if one exists and a first set of small tickets.
  2. Shadowing. The developer ships small fixes, learns the codebase and works through review with your senior developer or tech lead.
  3. Owning tasks. They pick up full features on their own, estimate their work and join planning like any team member.

Who a mid-level developer fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits teams with a defined product and a backlog of features and integrations, and businesses whose operations run on software that keeps needing new connections.

If your backlog is mostly small updates and content changes, a junior developer covers it. If no one owns architecture and code quality, hire a remote tech lead first or alongside.

For more than one developer, see IT staffing. To hand off a full build or ongoing upkeep, see custom app development and application maintenance.

faq.q: What can I expect when I hire a mid-level developer versus a junior?
faq.a: A mid-level developer can take a feature from ticket to release with light review. A junior needs smaller, well-defined tasks and closer guidance.

faq.q: Do I need a technical person to manage a mid-level developer?
faq.a: It helps. Someone should set priorities and review the code, either your own senior developer or a tech lead.

/casper-va/network-eng.add:
What a cloud network engineer handles day to day

  • Designing virtual networks, subnets and routing in AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.
  • Setting up and maintaining VPNs for remote staff and links between offices and the cloud.
  • Managing firewall rules and security groups so only the right traffic gets through.
  • Configuring DNS, load balancers and certificates.
  • Troubleshooting slow or dropped connections and tracing them to a cause.
  • Keeping network diagrams and change records current.

Tools a cloud network engineer commonly uses

Cloud network engineers commonly work with AWS VPC, Azure Virtual Network, Google Cloud networking, firewall and VPN platforms such as Fortinet, Palo Alto or WireGuard, infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform, and monitoring tools that watch latency and uptime.

How the first weeks with a cloud network engineer usually go

  1. Setup. You share current diagrams if you have them, cloud console access and the problems that prompted the hire.
  2. Shadowing. The engineer maps what exists, documents it and reviews findings with you before changing anything.
  3. Owning tasks. Changes go through an agreed process with rollback plans, and the engineer takes over day-to-day network care.

Who a cloud network engineer fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits companies with cloud workloads, multiple sites or a remote workforce whose network has grown without a plan, and teams moving more systems to the cloud.

If most problems are user-level, like logins, apps and laptops, hire a remote IT support engineer. If you need threat monitoring and compliance work more than network design, hire a remote security engineer.

For a project-based approach, see IT infrastructure services, cloud migration and performance monitoring. Need more than one engineer? See cloud engineer staffing.

faq.q: When should I hire a cloud network engineer instead of general IT support?
faq.a: Hire a cloud network engineer when your problems involve connectivity, VPNs, routing or cloud network design. General IT support covers users, devices and software.

faq.q: Can a cloud network engineer work on our office network too?
faq.a: Yes, for anything that can be configured remotely, such as firewalls, VPNs and switches with remote management. Physical cabling and hardware swaps need someone on site.

/casper-va/perf-marketing.add:
What a PPC specialist handles day to day

  • Building search campaigns around buying-intent keywords and cutting the ones that waste spend.
  • Adding negative keywords from the search terms report on a regular schedule.
  • Writing ad variations and testing headlines, offers and landing pages against each other.
  • Checking that conversion tracking, call tracking and form tracking all fire correctly.
  • Adjusting bids and budgets by campaign, device, location and time of day.
  • Reporting on cost per lead and lead quality, not just clicks.

Tools a PPC specialist commonly uses

PPC specialists commonly work in Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, Meta Ads Manager and LinkedIn Campaign Manager, plus Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, call tracking tools and landing page builders.

How the first weeks with a PPC specialist usually go

  1. Setup. You grant access to ad accounts and analytics. The specialist audits structure, tracking and recent spend.
  2. Shadowing. They review results with you, fix tracking first and agree on a test plan before touching budgets.
  3. Owning tasks. They manage campaigns daily and send a weekly report on spend, leads and the next tests.

Who a PPC specialist fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits businesses already running paid ads that want closer daily attention, and teams ready to launch ads with a clear offer and a working landing page.

If you need someone to decide whether ads should be the channel at all, start with a virtual marketing manager. If your ads keep stalling because creative is stale, add a virtual graphic designer.

For a managed program, see PPC management and social media advertising. If clicks don’t turn into leads, the issue is often the page, which is where conversion optimization helps.

faq.q: When should I hire a PPC specialist instead of running ads myself?
faq.a: Hire a PPC specialist when ads need daily attention you can’t give, or when spend is rising without a clear link to leads. A specialist watches search terms, tracking and tests that owners often skip.

faq.q: Does a PPC specialist control my ad budget?
faq.a: They manage spend inside the limits you set. Budget changes beyond those limits come to you for approval.

faq.q: Who owns the ad accounts?
faq.a: You do. The specialist works in your accounts with manager access, so the history and data stay with your business.

/casper-va/pm.add:
What a project manager handles day to day

  • Turning goals into a project plan with milestones, owners and dates.
  • Running sprint planning, stand-ups and retrospectives.
  • Keeping the project board current so anyone can see what is done and what is stuck.
  • Chasing blockers across your team, vendors and clients.
  • Sending clients and leadership regular status updates with clear risks.
  • Managing scope changes so new requests don’t quietly push deadlines.

Tools a project manager commonly uses

Project managers commonly use Jira, Asana, ClickUp, Monday or Trello, Slack or Teams, shared docs, Gantt or timeline views, and meeting tools. Many keep a simple risk and decision log alongside the board.

How the first weeks with a project manager usually go

  1. Setup. You share active projects, deadlines, team members and how work is tracked today.
  2. Shadowing. The PM attends existing meetings, meets each team member and cleans up the project board.
  3. Owning tasks. They run the meetings, own status updates and come to you only with decisions and escalations.

Who a project manager fits, and when to hire someone else

A virtual project manager fits agencies, software teams and service businesses running several projects at once with distributed people, where deadlines slip because no one owns follow-up.

If the projects need technical decisions more than coordination, hire a remote tech lead. If what you need is help with your own calendar and inbox, an executive assistant fits better.

For short-term or project-based teams, see project staffing. If you want the full build managed for you, see custom app development.

faq.q: Can a virtual project manager run client-facing meetings?
faq.a: Yes. Many PMs run client status calls, share updates and manage change requests, with you joining for key decisions.

faq.q: Does a project manager need to be technical?
faq.a: Not deeply, but they should understand how your team works. A PM on a software team should know the basics of how software gets built and released.

/casper-va/qa.add:
What a QA engineer handles day to day

  • Writing test cases from tickets and user stories before features are finished.
  • Running regression tests before each release so old features don’t break.
  • Testing across browsers, phones and screen sizes.
  • Writing clear bug reports with steps, screenshots and expected results.
  • Building and maintaining automated tests for the flows that matter most, like sign-up, checkout and forms.
  • Re-testing fixes and confirming releases are ready to ship.

Tools a QA engineer commonly uses

QA engineers commonly use test management tools like TestRail or Zephyr, issue trackers like Jira, automation frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress or Selenium, Postman for API tests, and real-device or browser testing services.

How the first weeks with a QA engineer usually go

  1. Setup. You provide staging access, current tickets and a walk-through of the product’s main user flows.
  2. Shadowing. The QA engineer tests the next release by hand, writes the first test cases and learns how your team reports bugs.
  3. Owning tasks. They own the release checklist, grow the automated test suite and sign off before deploys.

Who a QA engineer fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits teams shipping software regularly where developers test their own work, and businesses where bugs are reaching customers or staff.

If you need bugs fixed more than found, hire a junior developer or a mid-level developer. QA works best when there is a development team producing releases to test.

For a managed testing program, see software testing and QA services. For a larger team, see IT staffing.

faq.q: Should I hire a remote QA engineer for manual or automated testing?
faq.a: Most teams need both. Manual testing catches usability problems and new-feature bugs, while automated tests protect key flows on every release.

faq.q: Can a QA engineer test websites and workflows, not just apps?
faq.a: Yes. Forms, checkouts, CRM automations and email sequences can all be tested with the same approach as software.

/casper-va/sdr.add:
What an SDR handles day to day

  • Researching target accounts and finding the right decision-maker before reaching out.
  • Writing and sending personalized cold emails and LinkedIn messages in small, careful batches.
  • Making follow-up calls to prospects who opened, replied or asked to talk later.
  • Responding quickly to inbound leads and asking qualifying questions you defined.
  • Booking qualified meetings onto your calendar with notes on why the prospect is a fit.
  • Logging every touch in the CRM so your pipeline reflects real activity.

Tools an SDR commonly uses

SDRs commonly work in a CRM like HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive, email sequencing tools, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, a dialer, data lookup tools for contact details and a scheduling link. They also use your call scripts and objection notes.

How the first weeks with an SDR usually go

  1. Setup. You define your ideal customer, disqualifiers, offer and what counts as a qualified meeting. Domains and inboxes get warmed up and connected.
  2. Shadowing. The SDR listens to your sales calls, reviews past wins and losses, and sends first sequences for your approval.
  3. Owning tasks. The SDR runs outreach and qualification daily, and you meet weekly to review replies, meetings booked and what to change.

Who an SDR fits, and when to hire someone else

An outsourced SDR fits B2B companies with a clear offer and a closer, usually the owner or an account executive, who has more selling time than meetings on the calendar.

If you only need prospect lists built and verified, and your team already does the outreach, hire a lead generation VA instead. If you don’t yet know who your best customers are, start with sales pipeline strategy before adding outreach volume.

If you’d rather buy the outcome than manage a person, our appointment setting service runs the program for you. For a full outbound engine, see outbound prospecting and the B2B pipeline hub.

faq.q: What is the difference between an outsourced SDR and an appointment setting service?
faq.a: An outsourced SDR is a dedicated person you direct as part of your sales team. An appointment setting service is a managed program where we run the outreach and deliver booked meetings.

faq.q: Who closes the deals the SDR books?
faq.a: You or your sales team. The SDR’s job ends at a qualified meeting with clear notes, so the closer walks in prepared.

faq.q: Will an SDR send emails from my domain?
faq.a: Usually from a secondary domain you own, set up to protect your main domain’s email reputation. Replies route to the SDR and to you.

/casper-va/sec-eng.add:
What a security engineer handles day to day

  • Reviewing alerts from endpoint protection, email security and login monitoring, and separating real threats from noise.
  • Investigating suspicious sign-ins, phishing reports and unusual file activity.
  • Enforcing multi-factor authentication, least-privilege access and device policies.
  • Tracking patches and vulnerabilities and working with IT to close them.
  • Collecting evidence and documentation for compliance reviews and customer security questionnaires.
  • Keeping your incident response steps current and walking the team through them.

Tools a security engineer commonly uses

Level-2 security engineers commonly work with endpoint detection tools, SIEM or log platforms, Microsoft Defender or similar suites, vulnerability scanners, identity tools like Entra ID or Okta, and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA or PCI DSS as guides.

How the first weeks with a security engineer usually go

  1. Setup. You share your systems list, any compliance requirements, current security tools and past incidents.
  2. Shadowing. The engineer reviews alerts and settings without making changes, then presents a ranked list of gaps.
  3. Owning tasks. The engineer handles daily monitoring and works through the gap list with your approval on any change that affects users.

Who a security engineer fits, and when to hire someone else

This role fits businesses that handle payments, health records or client data, companies facing security questionnaires from customers, and IT teams with alerts but no one to review them.

If your environment is small and the basics like MFA, backups and patching aren’t in place yet, a remote IT support engineer can cover those first. If your exposure is mainly network design, hire a cloud network engineer.

For a managed program, see cybersecurity services, IT infrastructure and backup and recovery. The cyber risk assessment is a quick first check.

faq.q: What does L2 mean when you hire a remote security engineer?
faq.a: Level 2 means the engineer investigates and responds to alerts, not just watches for them. Complex incidents or forensics may need senior specialists on top.

faq.q: Can a remote security engineer help us pass a compliance audit?
faq.a: They can prepare evidence, fix gaps and document controls. The audit itself is performed by an independent auditor.

faq.q: Do we need a security engineer if we already have antivirus?
faq.a: Usually, yes, once you handle sensitive data. Antivirus is one layer, and someone still needs to review alerts, access and settings. Read why antivirus isn’t enough.

/casper-va/seo.add:
What an SEO specialist handles day to day

  • Mapping keywords to pages so each page targets one clear search intent.
  • Rewriting title tags, meta descriptions, headings and internal links on existing pages.
  • Fixing technical problems such as broken links, redirect chains, slow pages and indexing errors.
  • Keeping your Google Business Profile and local listings accurate and active.
  • Writing content briefs your writer can use for new pages and posts.
  • Reporting monthly on rankings, search traffic and the leads it produced.

Tools an SEO specialist commonly uses

SEO specialists commonly use Google Search Console, Google Analytics, crawlers like Screaming Frog, keyword tools such as Ahrefs or Semrush, PageSpeed Insights and your website’s content management system.

How the first weeks with an SEO specialist usually go

  1. Setup. You grant access to your site, Search Console and analytics. The specialist runs an audit of what exists today.
  2. Shadowing. They walk you through findings and agree on a priority list, starting with fixes that affect the pages that bring in leads.
  3. Owning tasks. They work the list steadily, publish changes on a schedule you approve and report on what moved.

Who an SEO specialist fits, and when to hire someone else

An SEO VA fits businesses with a working website that isn’t showing up for the searches their customers use, and teams who want SEO done consistently in-house rather than in occasional bursts.

If the gap is a lack of articles and page copy rather than technical or on-page work, hire a content writer. If you need someone to set strategy across SEO, ads and email, a virtual marketing manager fits better.

Prefer a managed program? See SEO services or local SEO. You can also start with the free local SEO checklist.

faq.q: What does an SEO virtual assistant need access to?
faq.a: Usually your website admin, Google Search Console, Google Analytics and Google Business Profile. Access is granted through your own accounts so you keep ownership.

faq.q: Should I hire an SEO VA or use an SEO agency?
faq.a: A dedicated SEO VA works only on your site and takes direction from you. An agency brings its own process and strategy, which helps if no one on your team can direct SEO work.

faq.q: Can an SEO specialist work on AI search visibility too?
faq.a: Yes. Clear answers, structured pages and accurate business listings help both search engines and AI assistants. Try the AI search readiness test to see where you stand.

/casper-va/social-media.add:
What a social media VA handles day to day

  • Planning a monthly content calendar for each platform you use.
  • Scheduling posts and adapting each one to fit the platform.
  • Answering comments and direct messages, and sending sales inquiries to the right person.
  • Sharing customer reviews, team photos and behind-the-scenes content you supply.
  • Watching for trends or local events worth joining.
  • Reporting monthly on reach, engagement and messages that turned into leads.

Tools a social media VA commonly uses

Social media VAs commonly use scheduling tools like Meta Business Suite, Buffer, Hootsuite or Later, Canva for quick graphics, short-form video editors like CapCut, and the native apps for Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok.

How the first weeks with a social media VA usually go

  1. Setup. You grant page access, share brand rules, photos and topics, and decide which messages the VA can answer.
  2. Shadowing. The VA drafts a first calendar and sample replies for your approval.
  3. Owning tasks. Posting and community replies run day to day, with you approving the calendar in advance instead of each post.

Who a social media VA fits, and when to hire someone else

A social media VA fits businesses that know social matters to their customers but post in bursts, and teams whose messages and comments go unanswered for too long.

If you need original graphics and video edits more than posting, hire a virtual graphic designer. If your goal is leads from paid social ads, a performance marketing specialist is the right role.

For a managed approach, see social media management and social media advertising.

faq.q: Can a social media virtual assistant make videos?
faq.a: Many can edit short clips from footage you record on your phone. Shooting on location is usually done by you or your team.

faq.q: How many platforms can one social media VA manage?
faq.a: It depends on posting volume and message traffic. Most businesses do better with two or three platforms done well than many done thinly.

/casper-va/tech-lead.add:
What a tech lead handles day to day

  • Choosing the architecture, frameworks and hosting for new builds, and writing down why.
  • Breaking big features into tasks other developers can pick up.
  • Reviewing pull requests for correctness, security and maintainability.
  • Setting coding standards, branching rules and deployment steps.
  • Pairing with developers on hard problems and unblocking the team.
  • Explaining technical tradeoffs to owners in plain terms before decisions are made.

Tools a tech lead commonly uses

Tech leads commonly work with GitHub or GitLab, CI/CD pipelines, cloud platforms like AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, issue trackers like Jira or Linear, diagramming tools and the language stack your product runs on.

How the first weeks with a tech lead usually go

  1. Setup. You share repository access, your roadmap and any existing documentation, and introduce the team.
  2. Shadowing. The tech lead reads the codebase, reviews recent work and writes up risks and quick wins.
  3. Owning tasks. They take over technical direction, run code review and planning with the developers, and report to you on progress and decisions.

Who a tech lead fits, and when to hire someone else

A remote tech lead fits companies with two or more developers and no senior technical owner, and founders building a product without a technical co-founder.

If the design is already set and you need features shipped, a mid-level developer is the better hire. If the trouble is deadlines and coordination rather than technical decisions, hire a virtual project manager.

Need a whole team? See IT staffing. If you’d rather hand off the build, see custom business app development or mobile app development.

faq.q: What is the difference between a tech lead and a senior developer?
faq.a: A tech lead owns technical decisions and guides other developers. A senior developer may write excellent code but isn’t necessarily responsible for the team’s direction.

faq.q: Can I hire a remote tech lead to review an outside agency’s work?
faq.a: Yes. A tech lead can review code, architecture and estimates from a vendor and tell you plainly where the risks are.

/casper-va/virtual-assistant.add:
What a general VA handles day to day

  • Sorting the inbox each morning: filing, flagging what needs you and drafting routine replies for your approval.
  • Booking and moving meetings, sending reminders and keeping one calendar that reflects reality.
  • Keeping shared drives tidy with a naming system everyone can follow.
  • Entering new contacts, orders or form submissions into the right system.
  • Chasing simple follow-ups: unsigned documents, missing paperwork, unanswered vendor emails.
  • Writing short end-of-day notes on what got done and what is waiting on you.

Tools a general VA commonly uses

General VAs commonly work in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, a shared calendar, a file system like Google Drive, Dropbox or SharePoint, and a task tool such as Asana, Trello or ClickUp. Your VA works inside your accounts with the access you grant, so nothing lives on a separate system you can’t see.

How the first weeks with a general VA usually go

  1. Setup. You share logins through a password manager, a list of recurring tasks and a few examples of how you like emails written.
  2. Shadowing. Your VA drafts and you approve. This is where tone, filing rules and “ask me first” items get settled.
  3. Owning tasks. Routine items move to the VA fully, and you shift to reviewing the daily summary instead of each task.

Who a general VA fits, and when to hire someone else

A general VA fits owners and small teams who lose hours to email, scheduling and file clutter and want one steady person to take it off their plate.

If you need someone to protect a busy leader’s time, manage stakeholders and prepare board-level materials, hire a virtual executive assistant. If the main job is high-volume record updates, a data entry specialist is the better match. Not sure which role you need? Our hiring guide walks through it.

Some repetitive admin work can be automated instead of staffed. We often pair a VA with AI automation so the person handles judgment calls and the system handles the copy-paste.

faq.q: What is the difference between a virtual administrative assistant and an executive assistant?
faq.a: A virtual administrative assistant handles routine email, calendar and file work for one person or a small team. An executive assistant supports a leader directly, handles sensitive communication and coordinates with outside stakeholders.

faq.q: Can a general VA work for more than one person on my team?
faq.a: Yes, as long as priorities are clear. We suggest naming one person who sets the VA’s priorities so requests don’t compete.

faq.q: How do I share passwords safely with a VA?
faq.a: Use a business password manager that lets you share access without revealing the password and revoke it anytime. Avoid sending credentials by email or chat.

/caspercare.add:
What a CasperCare plan covers

CasperCare is ongoing care for a website that is already live. Each plan is set in a written scope, so you know which items are included for your site. A plan typically covers:

  • Updates: core, theme and plugin updates applied on a regular schedule, with a backup taken before updates and a check of key pages afterward.
  • Backups: automated backups stored off your web server, with a set retention period and test restores so a backup is known to work.
  • Uptime monitoring: automated checks that alert us when your site stops responding, so the cause can be investigated.
  • Security monitoring: malware scans, login protection, firewall rules and patching of known vulnerabilities in the software your site runs.
  • SEO maintenance: Search Console review, broken link and redirect fixes, indexing checks and alerts when important pages drop out of Google's index.
  • Speed checks: regular tests of key pages so slowdowns from new plugins or large images are caught.
  • A monthly care report listing updates applied, backups run, issues found and what was done about them.

How CasperCare starts

  1. Fit call. We learn what your site runs on, who hosts it and what it does for your business.
  2. Onboarding review. We take a full backup, check current versions, scan for malware and list anything that needs fixing before regular care begins.
  3. Setup. Monitoring, backups and security tools are configured, and logins are stored securely.
  4. Regular care. Updates, scans and checks run on the plan's schedule.
  5. Monthly report. You get a plain-language summary and any recommendations, such as an outdated plugin worth replacing.

What's outside a care plan

Care plans keep an existing site healthy; they are not a redesign or a content service. New pages, new features and larger rebuilds are quoted separately through website development. Deeper speed work is handled through speed optimization, and ranking growth through SEO services. If your whole office needs IT and security support, not just the website, see managed IT and cybersecurity.

Who it fits

CasperCare fits businesses whose website brings in leads or sales and who don't have someone on staff checking updates, backups and security. It is also a good fit after we build a site for you, so it stays the way it launched. If you run a simple site that rarely changes, ask on the fit call whether a lighter plan makes more sense. To see how your site stands today, try the free website grader.

faq.q: Do I need website maintenance services if my site was just built?
faq.a: Yes. New sites still need software updates, backups and security monitoring, and problems are easier to prevent than to fix after a break-in or crash.

faq.q: Does CasperCare work with a site CasperB2B didn't build?
faq.a: Often, yes. We start with an onboarding review of the site, its hosting and its software, then tell you what needs fixing before regular care begins.

faq.q: What happens if my site goes down?
faq.a: Uptime monitoring alerts us when the site stops responding, and we investigate the cause, restore from backup if needed and note what happened in your care report.

/services/ai-chatbots.add:
What you get

  • A chatbot on your website styled to match your brand, set up on the pages where visitors usually have questions.
  • A knowledge base you approve: your services, service area, hours, booking rules and answers to common questions, written so the bot answers the way your team would.
  • Clear limits. The bot is told what it must not do, such as quoting prices you haven't approved, giving medical or legal advice or making promises about timing.
  • Lead capture and booking that collects name, contact details and job details, then offers times from your calendar.
  • Handoff to a person by text or email when a conversation needs your team.
  • Conversation logs you can review, so you see what people ask and where the bot needs better answers.

How an AI chatbot project works

  1. Fit call. We confirm what you want the bot to do and which pages it belongs on.
  2. Gather your content. We collect your FAQs, service pages, policies and booking rules.
  3. Draft and test. We build the bot and test it with real questions, tricky questions and off-topic questions.
  4. Your review. You try it, flag wrong or awkward answers, and approve it for launch.
  5. Launch and connect. The bot goes live with your calendar, CRM and handoff alerts connected.
  6. Tune. We review conversation logs and update answers as your services and questions change.

What we need from you

Your current FAQs and service details, rules for booking, the questions you never want the bot to answer, access to your calendar and CRM, and who should get handoff alerts. When something changes, like new hours or a new service, tell us so the knowledge base stays current.

Who it fits, and when it doesn't

Chatbots fit businesses that get the same questions over and over, lose after-hours website visitors or want leads qualified before a call. They are the wrong fit if most of your customers call rather than browse, or if every inquiry needs a custom conversation from the start; in that case, missed call text back or a customer service assistant may help more. For the basics, read what is an AI chatbot and do I need one. Chatbots are part of our wider AI automation work, and leads they capture can flow into your email follow-up.

faq.q: Will AI chatbot services give my customers wrong answers?
faq.a: The bot answers from a knowledge base you approve and is told to hand off rather than guess. We test it before launch and review conversation logs afterward to fix weak answers.

faq.q: Can the chatbot book appointments into my existing calendar?
faq.a: Yes, when your calendar or booking tool supports a connection. We confirm this on the fit call and set it up during launch.

faq.q: Who can see the chatbot conversations?
faq.a: You can review the conversation logs, and contact details collected by the bot go to your CRM or inbox. We set access so only your team sees them.

/services/analytics-data.add:
Questions your dashboard should answer

A useful marketing dashboard answers a short list of business questions: Where did this month's leads come from? Which leads became customers? What did each channel cost per customer? Which pages bring in calls? We build reports around those questions first, then add detail only where it helps a decision. If a number doesn't change what you do, it stays off the main view; we explain why in what are vanity metrics.

How marketing analytics setup works

  1. Audit. We review your current GA4 property, Google Tag Manager, ad platform tracking and CRM fields to see what is missing, broken or counted twice.
  2. Tracking plan. A written list of every event and conversion to track, such as calls, form fills, bookings and purchases, and where each is captured.
  3. Implementation. We set up GA4 events, Tag Manager tags, call tracking, UTM rules for your campaigns and consent settings where required.
  4. CRM connection. Lead source data is passed into your CRM so closed deals can be traced back to the campaign that started them.
  5. Dashboard build. A Looker Studio or similar dashboard with the views you agreed on, shared with your team.
  6. Walkthrough. We show you how to read it and set a regular review rhythm.

What we need from you

Admin access to your website, GA4, Google Tag Manager, ad accounts and CRM, a list of what counts as a lead and as a sale in your business, and the questions you most want answered. If your CRM doesn't record where leads came from, we will help you add that field and the habit of filling it in.

Who it fits, and when it doesn't

Analytics work fits businesses spending on ads or SEO that can't say which channel brings in customers, or that have tracking set up by several past vendors. It is the wrong first step if you have almost no traffic or leads yet; get lead flow going first with SEO or PPC. Clean data then feeds conversion optimization and pipeline reporting covered in sales pipeline tracking. To check whether your channels pay off, try the LTV to CAC calculator.

faq.q: Do marketing analytics services work with my existing CRM?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Most CRMs can store lead source and campaign data, and we confirm the connection method during the audit before building anything.

faq.q: Why don't my GA4 numbers match my ad platform numbers?
faq.a: Each platform counts conversions with its own rules and time windows, and ad blockers or consent settings can hide some visits. We document these differences so your team knows which number to use for each decision.

faq.q: Who owns the tracking and dashboards?
faq.a: Your business does. Everything is built in accounts you own, and we work with access you grant.

/services/brand-style-guides.add:
What the finished style guide includes

Logo rules

Approved versions (full, stacked, icon), minimum sizes, clear space, which version to use on dark and light backgrounds, and examples of what not to do.

Color system

Primary and accent colors with HEX, RGB and CMYK codes, plus guidance on which colors to use for buttons, text and backgrounds so text stays readable.

Typography

Fonts for headings and body text, sizes for web and print, and free fallback fonts for tools that don't have your brand fonts.

Voice and examples

How your business sounds, words you use and avoid, and sample lines for an ad, a social post and an email.

You receive the guide as a shareable PDF and a folder of logo files, color swatches and templates for the pieces you use most, such as social posts or letterhead.

How we build it

  1. Collect what exists. We gather your logo files, past marketing, website and anything vendors have made for you.
  2. Find the drift. We point out where colors, fonts and logo versions don't match today.
  3. Set the rules. We draft the guide, keeping what works and fixing what doesn't, without changing your logo unless you ask.
  4. Review. You review the draft, and we revise it based on your notes.
  5. Hand off. You get the final PDF and asset folder, ready to send to anyone who makes marketing for you.

What we need from you

The original logo files if you have them, examples of marketing you like and dislike, a few words that describe how you want customers to see you, and the names of any vendors who will use the guide. If your only logo is a low-quality image, we can recreate it as a clean vector file or point you to logo design.

Who it fits, and how it connects

A style guide fits businesses with more than one person or vendor creating marketing, businesses about to launch a new website or ad campaign, and owners who notice their materials all look slightly different. If you are still deciding on a name or logo, do that first. The guide makes our graphic design, social media and website work faster and more consistent. To experiment with colors and fonts on your own first, try the free brand kit generator.

faq.q: How long is a typical brand style guide?
faq.a: Long enough to cover logo, color, type and voice rules with examples, and short enough that a vendor will actually read it. Most small businesses need a focused guide, not a thick manual.

faq.q: Do brand style guide services include a new logo?
faq.a: Not by default. The guide documents your current logo and sets rules for it; a new or refreshed logo is a separate logo design project.

faq.q: Can my team update the style guide later?
faq.a: Yes. You receive the files, and we can add sections later, such as rules for video, signage or a new product line.

/services/business-listings.add:
What listings management includes

  • A listings audit that finds where your business appears today and flags wrong names, old addresses, dead phone numbers, missing hours and duplicates.
  • One master record of your exact business name, address, phone, website, hours, categories and description, approved by you, so every listing matches.
  • Claiming and verification of your profiles on Google, Apple Maps, Bing, Yelp and the main data sources other directories copy from.
  • Corrections and duplicate removal, including merge or removal requests where a platform allows them.
  • Ongoing monitoring for changes you didn't make, with fixes when someone suggests a wrong edit.
  • Holiday and hours updates pushed out when your schedule changes.

How it works

  1. Gather your details. We confirm the exact format of your name and address, including suite numbers, and your primary category.
  2. Audit. We search for your current listings, old addresses and old phone numbers to find every version out there.
  3. Claim and correct. We claim profiles, fix the data and request removal of duplicates. Some platforms need a postcard, call or video to verify, which we walk you through.
  4. Monitor. We watch for changes and send a monthly listing health report.

What we need from you

Your correct business details, any old addresses, phone numbers or business names you have used, logins for profiles you already own and a person who can receive verification codes or postcards. If you are a service-area business without a public storefront, tell us so your address is handled the way the platforms require.

Who it fits, and how it connects

This fits any local business that has moved, changed phone numbers, rebranded or has more than one location. It also fits if you have never checked your listings at all. Listings are one part of local search; for the rest, see local SEO services and why your business isn't showing on Google Maps. Reviews on those listings are handled through reputation management. To check your own setup, use the free local SEO checklist or read how to get your business on Google Maps. Unsure what a term means? Our local SEO glossary explains it.

faq.q: What does business listings management cost?
faq.a: It is quoted on the 15-minute fit call based on how many locations you have and how much cleanup your current listings need.

faq.q: Can business listings management remove a duplicate Google listing?
faq.a: We request removal or merging through the platform's own process. The platform makes the final decision, but correct verified data on your main listing helps the request.

faq.q: Do I need listings management if I already have a Google Business Profile?
faq.a: Google checks other directories to confirm your details, so wrong or old information on Apple Maps, Bing, Yelp and data sources can still hurt you even with a good Google profile.

/services/cloud-computing.add:
What a cloud migration covers

  • An inventory of your servers, shared drives, email, line-of-business apps, user accounts and devices, with notes on what moves, what gets replaced and what gets retired.
  • A migration plan with the order of moves, a cutover window outside your busy hours and a rollback step if something doesn't work.
  • Email and file moves into Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, with folder permissions rebuilt so people see only what they should.
  • Security settings: multi-factor authentication, admin account separation and sharing rules set before users log in.
  • Backups of cloud email and files, since the provider keeping your data online is not the same as you having a restorable copy.
  • User training on where files live now, how to share them and how to sign in on phones and laptops.

How the move works

  1. Discovery. We review what you run today and talk with the people who use it.
  2. Plan and scope. You get a written plan and a signed scope before any data moves.
  3. Prepare. We set up the cloud tenant, accounts, security and backups first.
  4. Pilot. A few users move first so we catch problems early.
  5. Cutover. The rest of the team moves in the planned window, and we check mail flow, file access and apps.
  6. Clean up. Old servers are decommissioned or kept as a temporary fallback, and you get documentation of the new setup.

What we need from you

Admin passwords handed over through a secure method we agree on, a list of the software your team uses each day, a contact who can approve the cutover date and any compliance needs that apply to your industry. Older apps that only run on a local server need special attention, so tell us about them early.

Who it fits, and when it doesn't

Cloud migration fits small offices running an aging server, teams that work from home or job sites, and businesses that want email and files backed up off-site. It may not fit if a key app has no cloud version and can't be hosted, or if your internet connection is too slow to work from the cloud; we will flag both during discovery. After the move, ongoing support comes through managed IT, protection through cybersecurity services, and restore planning through backup and recovery. Larger network and server work is covered under IT infrastructure. Not sure if you need outside help? Read do I need an IT person.

faq.q: What does cloud migration services for small business typically move?
faq.a: Email, shared files, user accounts and business apps that have cloud versions. Each item is listed in the inventory with a plan to move, replace or retire it.

faq.q: Is my data safe during a cloud migration?
faq.a: Data is copied, checked and backed up before the old system is turned off, and security settings like multi-factor authentication are in place before users log in.

faq.q: Do I still need backups if my files are in Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace?
faq.a: Yes. The provider keeps the service running, but deleted or encrypted files may not be recoverable without a separate backup, so we set one up as part of the move.

/services/conversion-optimization.add:
What you get from a CRO engagement

  • A conversion audit of your key pages, listing each problem we find, why it costs you leads and the fix, ranked by expected impact and effort.
  • Tracking that counts real leads: calls, form submissions, bookings and chat starts set up as conversions, so changes are measured against outcomes.
  • Page changes made for you: rewritten headlines and offers, shorter forms, clearer buttons, click-to-call on mobile and reviews placed near the decision point.
  • Before-and-after tests on the pages that matter most, run long enough to read honestly.
  • A written summary of what changed, what it did and what to try next.

How conversion rate optimization works

  1. Measure. We confirm your analytics and conversion tracking are accurate. Bad data leads to bad decisions, so this comes first.
  2. Find the leaks. We review analytics, heatmaps and session recordings to see where visitors hesitate or leave.
  3. Prioritize. We rank fixes by likely effect on leads and how hard they are to ship.
  4. Fix and test. Clear bugs and broken forms get fixed right away. Bigger changes, like a new offer or layout, are tested against the current version.
  5. Review and repeat. We read the results with you and pick the next round of changes.

What we need from you

Admin access to your website and analytics, a sense of which leads turn into good customers, and honest answers about your offer and pricing so the copy matches how you actually sell. If you track leads in a CRM, access to it lets us see which pages produce customers, not just inquiries.

Who it fits, and when to fix something else first

CRO pays off when you already get steady traffic but too few calls or forms. If your site gets very little traffic, tests take too long to read; start with SEO or PPC. If leads come in but don't turn into appointments, the problem is often follow-up; see turning inquiries into appointments. A slow site can also hurt conversions, which our speed optimization work addresses, and accurate tracking comes from our analytics setup. For a quick self-check, run your site through the free website grader.

faq.q: How long before conversion rate optimization services show results?
faq.a: Fixes like broken forms or missing click-to-call can help as soon as they ship. Tested changes need enough visitors to read clearly, so the timeline depends on your traffic.

faq.q: Do I need a website redesign to improve conversions?
faq.a: Usually not. Most gains come from clearer offers, shorter forms, better mobile layout and trust signals on the pages you already have.

faq.q: What counts as a conversion on a small business website?
faq.a: Any action that starts a sales conversation: a phone call, a form submission, a booked appointment or a chat that leaves contact details.

/services/custom-apps.add:
When a custom app makes sense

Most small businesses should use off-the-shelf software first. A custom app is worth building when your team keeps the same data in three places, when a spreadsheet has grown into something only one person understands, or when your customers need a way to see status, upload files or approve work without calling you. If an existing tool does 90 of the 100 things you need, we will usually tell you to keep it and connect it instead, which is often an automation project rather than a new app.

How custom business app development works

  1. Workflow mapping. We sit with the people who do the work and write down each step, who touches it and where it breaks.
  2. Written scope. A plain-language document listing screens, user roles, data, integrations and what is out of scope. Work starts from that signed scope.
  3. Clickable prototype. You see the screens and flow before code is written, so changes are cheap.
  4. Build in stages. We ship the core workflow first, then add features in planned rounds you can test as they land.
  5. Testing and launch. Your team tests with real data, we fix what they find, then we move you over and train your users.
  6. Support. Updates, fixes and new features as your process changes.

What you get

A working app

Web-based screens for each user role, with logins and permissions set by who needs to see what.

Your data, organized

A structured database that replaces scattered spreadsheets, with exports when you need them.

Connections to your tools

Links to your CRM, accounting, email or calendar so data entered once shows up everywhere it should.

Documentation

Notes on how the app is built and how to use it, so you are not dependent on memory.

What we need from you

One decision-maker, access to the people who do the work today, sample data and the reports you wish you had. Real examples of real jobs make the scope accurate. You can see apps we have built, such as NextWeigh and CarSales AI, on our portfolio page.

Related services

If you need a phone app in the app stores, see mobile app development. For ongoing fixes after launch, see application maintenance, and for structured testing before a release, see software testing.

faq.q: How do you decide what a custom business app development project includes?
faq.a: We map your workflow with the people who do it, then write a signed scope listing screens, user roles, data and integrations. Anything not in the scope is quoted separately before it is built.

faq.q: Will I own the app and its data?
faq.a: Your business data is yours, and ownership of the code and hosting accounts is spelled out in the scope before work begins.

faq.q: Can a custom app connect to the software I already use?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Most CRMs, accounting tools, calendars and email platforms offer ways to connect, and we confirm each connection during scoping.

/services/email-marketing.add:
What we set up for you

New lead sequence

A short series that sends after someone inquires: a thank-you with what happens next, answers to common questions, proof of your work and a clear way to book.

Past customer reactivation

Emails to people who bought before, timed to when they are likely to need you again, such as seasonal service, renewals or annual checkups.

Newsletter template

A reusable, mobile-friendly layout in your brand, plus a simple monthly content plan so it actually goes out.

List cleanup and signup forms

Duplicates and bad addresses removed, contacts tagged by service or status, and signup forms on your site that feed the right list.

How email marketing works with us

  1. Audit your list and tools. We look at where contacts live today, how they were collected and what platform you use.
  2. Fix sending basics. We check SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for your domain so your emails are more likely to reach the inbox instead of spam.
  3. Map the sequences. You approve the trigger, timing and goal for each email before we write it.
  4. Write and design. We write the emails in your voice and build them in your brand template.
  5. Launch and connect. Sequences are tied to your forms and CRM so they start on their own.
  6. Review monthly. We look at opens, clicks, replies and bookings, then adjust subject lines, timing and offers.

What we need from you

Access to your email platform or CRM, your current contact list and where it came from, your top services and common questions, and someone to answer replies. Only email people who gave you permission or are existing customers; we will help you sort that out during the audit. If you want examples first, read email automation examples for small business.

How it connects to your other marketing

Email is the follow-up layer for leads from ads, search and social. It works best inside a CRM, which we set up through our automation services. If leads go quiet after the first call, see why leads go cold. Email is the wrong first step if you have no list and no steady inquiries yet; build lead flow first, then add email to keep it.

faq.q: Which platform do your email marketing services for small business use?
faq.a: We usually work in the email platform or CRM you already have. If you don't have one, we recommend one that fits your size and connects to your website forms.

faq.q: How often should a small business send emails?
faq.a: Automated sequences send based on what each person does. For newsletters, a steady monthly schedule you can keep up beats frequent sends that stop after a few months.

faq.q: Why do my emails go to spam?
faq.a: Common causes are missing SPF, DKIM or DMARC records, old or purchased lists and spammy wording. We check and fix the domain records as part of setup.

/services/graphic-design.add:
What you receive with every design request

  • Source files you own, plus export formats for web (PNG, JPG, SVG, WebP) and print-ready PDFs with bleed and crop marks when the piece is going to a printer.
  • Correct sizes for each placement: feed, story and ad sizes for social, banner sizes for your website and Google ads, and the dimensions your printer asks for.
  • Revision rounds set in the scope for each piece, so feedback is collected in one place instead of trickling in.
  • Organized delivery in a shared folder labeled by campaign and date, so your team can find last spring's flyer without asking.

How a design project runs

  1. Brief. You tell us what the piece is for, where it will appear, the one action you want people to take and any deadline.
  2. Brand check. We pull your colors, fonts and logo files. If you don't have them written down, we suggest a brand style guide first.
  3. First draft. One clear direction built around your message, not a pile of options to sort through.
  4. Revisions. You mark up changes in one round of comments, and we deliver the next version.
  5. Final files. Exports for every size and format, saved to your folder and ready for your ads, website or printer.

What we need from you

Your logo in the best format you have, any brand colors or fonts, real photos of your team or work, and the exact wording for offers, phone numbers and dates. Getting the copy right before design starts is the single biggest way to keep revisions short.

Who it fits, and when it doesn't

It fits small businesses that need ad creatives, social graphics, brochures or sales decks on a regular basis without hiring a full-time designer. If you don't have a logo yet, start with logo design. If you need a designer working inside your team every day, look at a dedicated virtual graphic designer. Ad creatives are built to work with our PPC management and social ads campaigns, and you can sketch a starting palette with the free brand kit generator.

faq.q: Do I own the files from your graphic design services?
faq.a: Yes. You receive the source files and every export, and you can use them anywhere your business needs them.

faq.q: Can you design print pieces and send them to my printer?
faq.a: We prepare print-ready PDFs with bleed and crop marks to your printer's specs. You place the print order with the printer you choose.

faq.q: What makes graphic design services for small business different from a template tool?
faq.a: Templates give you a starting layout; a designer builds the piece around your offer, your audience and the placement, and keeps it consistent with everything else you publish.

/services/social-media-ads.add:
How a social ad campaign is built

  1. Offer and goal. We agree on one clear offer, such as a free estimate, a consultation or a seasonal service, and the action that counts as a lead.
  2. Tracking first. We install or check the Meta pixel, the LinkedIn Insight Tag and conversion events so results are measured from day one.
  3. Audiences. We build audiences by location, interests or job titles, plus retargeting lists of site visitors and lookalikes of past customers when your data allows.
  4. Creative and copy. Several ad versions with different hooks, images and short videos, sized for feeds and stories.
  5. Lead routing. In-app form leads go straight to your CRM, inbox or phone so someone follows up while interest is fresh.
  6. Weekly tuning. We pause weak ads, refresh tired creative and move budget toward the audiences producing leads.

What you see in your reports

Each report lists spend, leads, cost per lead and which ads and audiences produced them. When your CRM is connected, we also show which leads became booked jobs, so you judge the campaign on customers, not clicks. You own the ad account, the pixel and the audiences; we work inside them with access you grant.

What we need from you
